questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had visited Iceland before, and loved the country. The nature is stunning, as well as friendly people and a safe environment. In terms of my studies, the country seemed to offer interesting aspects.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The university was a great place, did however feel lonely in the beginning.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fine, I had to go to the University to gain access to the University intranet. After that it was quite simple.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: When arriving at the university, I found the student service (was a little confused about the place), and they gave me my password for the intranet, as well as a little information. However, mostly received e-mails.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy through HousingAnywhere. Remember to get an official contract.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Campus is quite far from the city center (15-20 min walk). I would have liked to stay on campus, because it seemed that more social events happened there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Generally quite expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Logged into an UGLA portal, and then had to choose courses. I had quite some trouble logging into the portal, since you had to use your university email (with a special ending). I also had some difficulties choosing courses that fit 30 ECTS. But in the end, the courses that I had were very relevant.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could email to XX at host uni (Name removed) the responsible person for exchange students. However, I ended up getting help from another exchange student in Denmark.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to start the process early, since it takes a while to figure it all out. Answering time from the University is also not very quick. And remember to get approval from your home university early as well.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was quite similar to the one at Copenhagen University.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There were more hours mandatory at the University. The final grade in a course is based on many activities throughout the course, not only a final exam (quizzes, many submissions, reports etc.). The exams were also mostly closed-book.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Cartography and map design 
Global Climate Change
Physical Geography 
The Arctic Circle 
Natural Hazards

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The Artic Circle is a course based on your attendance in the conference in October, and two papers afterwards. It is a really fun experience. 
I can also recommend the cartography course, if you want to learn QGIS. 
Global Climate Change had focus on both the physical processes and the societal/political/human aspects of climate change, which I also really enjoyed.
Physical geography had some field- and labwork regarding soil science, which were interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
The busses out of Reykjavik are quite expensive, and generally "tourist acitivities".
Eating out/coffee is expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
It is quite affordable to rent a car, especially if you are sharing it 5 people (remember to get insurance, the weather is wild!)
Chocolate and skyr is cheap (compared to DK), meat is really expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a choir, student associations and a gym, where there is some nice activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the gym, it is cheap and nice. And join "dog day" on Wednesdays, where a cute dog comes to visit from Red Cross.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on car trips to the Westfjords, Kerlingafjöll, Snæfellsness, Vestmannaeyar, the lava tunnel and see the glaciers. Go for horse riding or kayaking.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, since it is very similar to Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The local students were not always that keen to socialize with the exchange students. However, the other exchange students were very nice.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Less social activities than I am used to at home (I live in a social dorm, and my department at the University is also active).

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Friendly people, generally talkative if you start a conversation. Very chill and safe place.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Be ready to study a lot, for submissions, tests and closed book exam (however, very rewarding academically). Remember to study with friends, that makes it way more fun. 
2) Try to participate in activities, go on some trips etc. with people from early on. It is important to make some friends. Generally, find activities outside of University to do.
3) Keep in contact with friends and family at home - and ask them to come visit you. It had multible visits, and it was amazing.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There a lots of nice places to study at Campus, and also help to get from the student counselling, service etc. 
I had a little job as a "note taker", which can be recommended (remember to check your University e-mail).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Experiencing beautiful nature, got some really lovely friends from all over the world, and progressed academically.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Feeling lonely, especially in the beginning.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
